name: Multi-winner approval voting
summary: Count support for each candidate independently and elect the k largest totals. This maximizes total approved representatives, not proportional representation.
steps: Add count to every candidate approved on each ballot.
Order candidates by approval total, using the fixed candidate priority for a tied cutoff.
Elect the first k candidates.
variant: Approval voting (AV), also called approval bloc voting, with unrestricted approval subsets.
tieNotes: The simulation chooses exactly the requested number of candidates. Earlier IDs in candidates have priority when a count needs a tied choice; later IDs are eliminated first. tie reports a consequential tied decision, not extra seats or additional elected candidates. Mathematical properties of an unbroken correspondence may require different tie assumptions.
complexity: O(bm + m log m) with straightforward membership checks.
limits: Shared limits: 32 candidates, 10,000 ballot groups and 1,000,000 represented voters; see the API guide for numeric bounds.

name: Proportional approval voting (PAV)
summary: Evaluate whole committees using diminishing returns: a voter gets 1 point for a first approved representative, another 1/2 for a second, another 1/3 for a third, and so on.
steps: Enumerate all size-k committees.
For each ballot, count its approved committee members t and add count × (1 + 1/2 + … + 1/t).
Select a committee maximizing the total harmonic satisfaction.
variant: Exact harmonic PAV, not its sequential approximation. Rational arithmetic decides equal scores exactly.
tieNotes: The simulation chooses exactly the requested number of candidates. Earlier IDs in candidates have priority when a count needs a tied choice; later IDs are eliminated first. tie reports a consequential tied decision, not extra seats or additional elected candidates. Mathematical properties of an unbroken correspondence may require different tie assumptions.
complexity: O(binomial(m,k) × bm) straightforward exhaustive committee scoring.
limits: Exact committee enumeration is limited to 8 candidates, in addition to the shared API limits.

name: Single transferable vote (STV)
summary: Voters rank candidates. Quota winners retain enough vote weight for a seat, surplus weight transfers, and the lowest remaining candidate is eliminated when nobody reaches quota.
steps: Set the integer Droop quota to floor(N/(k+1)) + 1. Each ballot starts with weight 1.
Give each continuing ballot to its highest-ranked continuing candidate. Elect a quota-reaching candidate and transfer its surplus proportionally across all ballots currently assigned to it.
If nobody reaches quota, eliminate a lowest-total candidate and transfer those ballots. Elect all remaining candidates when they exactly fill the unfilled seats.

complexity: At most m selection or elimination rounds; straightforward repeated ranking scans cost O(bm²) arithmetic operations.

summary: Compare possible committees after transferring surplus votes of candidates common to both. Use those committee contests to resolve the election.
